# Vendored Packages

This directory contains source-vendored copies of the Cordis framework and its foundation libraries. They are copied into this monorepo instead of being depended on via npm, so that the harness fully owns its framework layer (auditable, patchable, pinned).

All vendored packages use the **`@deepseek-ai` scope** (`cordis` → `@deepseek-ai/cordis`, `@cordisjs/plugin-<x>` → `@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-<x>`). The manifest table records upstream versions and source commits; each package manifest carries its Harness release version and publication metadata. References to vendored packages use `workspace:~`, so local builds resolve the workspace packages and published ranges permit patch updates within the same minor version. Upstream MIT `LICENSE` files are preserved in each package directory.

This file covers the manifest, the local-modification log, and the procedure for **updating** an existing vendored package. To **add a new** one, see the cookbook guide: [docs/cookbook/adding-a-vendored-package.md](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-vendored-package.md).

The proposed [Cordis rc.11 upgrade plan](cordis-rc11-upgrade-plan.md) records the package scope, PR dependencies and intended disposition of the local modifications.

**Partial Loader sync:** the package baseline remains 1.0.0-rc.5. `loader/src/resolve.ts` and the bare-specifier fallback in `loader/src/config/tree.ts` use the resolver implementation from Cordis `v4.0.0-rc.11` (Loader 1.0.0-rc.8), and `loader/src/internal.ts` uses its runtime API detection, which classifies the internal module loader by its available module-job APIs instead of the Node major version; the Node compatibility matrix covers the detection. The [resolver adaptations](#resolver-adaptations) below record the local differences from that newer source.

Third-party dependencies of the vendored packages stay on npm: `@standard-schema/spec`, `js-yaml`, `chokidar`, `picomatch`, `@babel/code-frame`, `supports-color`, `node-addon-require-builtin`, `undici`, `file-type`, `mime-types`, `path-to-regexp`, `path-to-regexp-typed`, `protobufjs`, and the markdown parser closure `satori-element` gains for `<markdown>` expansion (`mdast-util-from-markdown`, `mdast-util-gfm`, `micromark-extension-gfm`).

Intentionally **not** vendored (verified unused by this set): `reggol`, `@cordisjs/utils`, `@cordisjs/unyaml` (dev-time YAML import hook only).

## Local modifications

Keep this log exhaustive — every divergence from upstream must be listed. Each entry has a stable ID: remove an entry when its divergence no longer exists, and never renumber or reuse IDs. The next new entry is V53.
- **V1 · `hmr/src/index.ts`**: removed the `./locales/en-US.yml` / `./locales/zh-CN.yml` imports, the `.i18n({...})` call on the `Config` schema, and the `src/locales/` directory. Rationale: those imports require a runtime YAML loader hook (`@cordisjs/unyaml`) that we do not vendor; the i18n texts only localize config descriptions.
- **V2 · All `package.json` files**: regenerated for Harness releases with scoped names, release versions, publication metadata, precise bundled-runtime and `lib/types/**/*.d.ts` / `.d.ts.map` file entries, source exports where applicable, and declaration metadata pointing at `lib/types`. References within the vendored set use `workspace:~`. HMR declares `esbuild` as a direct dev dependency for its imported `BuildFailure` type, and Loader requires `node-addon-require-builtin@^0.1.4` to match published app runtimes.
- **V3 · All `tsconfig.json` files**: regenerated to extend the repo-root `tsconfig.base.json`, emit TypeScript intermediates to `lib/types`, and declare project references.
- **V4 · Vendored TypeScript source internal specifiers**: changed local relative imports/exports from upstream's specifier shape to explicit `.ts` specifiers so TypeScript rewrites emitted JS to `.js` while declarations keep explicit, NodeNext-safe `.ts` specifiers. This includes `loader/src/config/isolate.ts` using `declare module './entry.ts'`. Type-only dependencies use `import type` or inline `type` modifiers so ESM output does not retain erased interfaces.
- **V5 · `schemastery/tsdown.config.ts` and `logger-console/tsdown.config.ts`**: ours, not upstream files — per-package build-shape overrides (dual ESM+CJS output; separate node/browser entries) for the repo-root tsdown build. They read the JS emitted under `lib/types` and then write the publish runtime entries under `lib/`. Like the regenerated tsconfigs, they are not part of the upstream sync surface.
- **V6 · `cordis/src/fiber.ts` lifecycle hardening**: locally closes three reentrant disposal gaps. An effect's owner-list wrapper is registered before its setup body runs, so an unload begun from inside setup awaits setup and every collected cleanup; synchronous setup failure removes the wrapper and rolls back collected cleanup. Async cleanup stays owner-visible until quiescence, and Cordis's internal effect composition joins an already-running cleanup while repeated public disposer calls retain their upstream single-shot result. Effect creation is rejected while the owner is `UNLOADING` (while `PENDING` and `LOADING` remain legal), preventing cleanup-time registrations from escaping the unload snapshot. Child fibers register and receive their parent-owned disposer before `internal/plugin` publication, resolve dependency declarations added by that notification before activation, drain effects attached while pending, and contain teardown-notification failures per observer so one callback cannot starve peers or interrupt ownership cleanup.
- **V7 · Cordis, Loader and Timer JSDoc enrichment**: added `@param`/`@returns` tags and contract documentation (disposal semantics, waterfall veto, bail conditions, error cases) across the public plugin-author surface — `Context` (class, statics, and the `Context` interface properties incl. `root`), module re-exports, shared utility helpers, `EventsService`, `Fiber`, `RegistryService`, `ReflectService`, `Service`, `LoggerService` and their `declare module './context.ts'` overloads. Loader documentation covers `loader/src/{index,internal,config/entry,config/group,config/isolate,config/tree,config/utils}.ts`, including entry ownership, tree mutation methods, and the `!!js` discriminator. Timer retains its local class and helper summaries; its README is local documentation because the upstream package has none. Comment-only; no code changes. Motivation: the website API-reference generator renders these docs and hard-errors on undocumented members. Retire this entry when the enrichment is upstreamed to the fork.
- **V8 · `include/src/index.ts` resilient file refresh and patch reapplication**: [#514](https://github.com/deepseek-harness/deepseek-harness/pull/514) validates a top-level entry array before caching parsed content, logs refresh failures, reapplies patches after file or Include-config edits, updates the Include config when it vetoes a restart, and uses `initial` only after `ENOENT`. These parse protections retain the running tree after an invalid file; plugin activation failures can leave a partially applied tree. Loader entry/group/tree mutations follow the pinned eager, non-transactional implementation and do not restore previous plugins or options. Covered by `packages/boot/app-boot/tests/{config-reload,user-patches}.spec.ts`.
- **V9 · `hmr/src/index.ts` module-watcher readiness and native paths**: realpath the existing watch base, classify framework modules and attach listeners before reporting readiness, and compare config paths using both canonical and configured spellings. This preserves Node module-cache identity across Windows short-name paths and filesystem aliases. The main watcher uses `ignoreInitial: true` so startup reads do not trigger another refresh; exact profile patch watching is owned by `packages/boot/hmr/src/watch-config.ts`. Covered by `packages/boot/hmr/tests/watch-config.spec.ts`.
- **V10 · Vendored Node-compatible TypeScript**: marked erased imports explicitly across `cordis`, `loader`, `include`, `hmr`, and `schemastery` so Node's native TypeScript transform does not request types as runtime exports. Schemastery's source uses an ESM default export and its package declares `type: module`. Conditional exports select `.mjs` for import and `.cjs` for require; without them, concurrent imports under module-hook hosts reach the CJS entry and can race its require of ESM Cosmokit (`ERR_REQUIRE_ESM_RACE_CONDITION`).
- **V11 · `include/src/index.ts` patch-semantics export**: extracted the private `applyPatches` body into the exported pure function `applyEntryPatches(data, patches, warn)` (the method delegates to it) and exported the `!!js` YAML dialect as `entryListSchema`, so `dsh --dump-config` composes and prints exactly what the include would mount without booting a tree. The entry list is deep-cloned when patches are present; without patches, the returned array retains the entry objects. Public patch and Include fields carry JSDoc for config tooling. Behavior-preserving for mounting; the extraction exists because config tooling must never reimplement (and drift from) the patch algorithm. `applyEntryPatches` also indexes each `insert`ed entry as it is added, so a later patch in the same list can configure or disable a row an earlier patch inserted; upstream built the id index once before the patch loop, leaving inserted rows silently unpatchable. That matters because `dsh` composes an empty profile root with each bundle's patch layer, the profile's and the home-level `cordis.patch.yml`, and any `--patch` overlays as sibling patch lists at one include level — patches never cross an include boundary, so surface-only rows would otherwise be unreachable from user config. Covered by `packages/boot/app-boot/tests/config-reload.spec.ts`.
- **V13 · `include/src/index.ts` `writeTask` type**: widened the optional `writeTask?: NodeJS.Timeout` property to `NodeJS.Timeout | undefined` — the debounced writer assigns `undefined` on flush, which `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` rejects on a plain optional. Type-only; no behavior change.
- **V14 · `include/src/index.ts` durable debounced writes**: serialized and tracked config-file writes, retried transient `EACCES`/`EBUSY`/`EPERM` rename failures with a bounded backoff, observed asynchronous timer rejections, and drained writes before and after child removal during Include teardown. The first drain preserves an existing terminal write failure even if child removal schedules a later write. Missing-file initialization awaits the write and forces a fresh parse before mounting the initial entries. Windows can briefly retain a destination handle after a Loader child disposes; the upstream fire-and-forget rename escaped as an unhandled rejection and could lose the persisted `disabled` state. A terminal failure is logged by the asynchronous writer and remains on the queue so `Include.stop()` rethrows it instead of silently declaring persistence complete; Cordis's ordinary fiber teardown retains its separate error-containment contract. Covered by `packages/host/directory-picker-auto/tests/loader-composition.spec.ts` with injected transient and terminal rename failures.
- **V15 · Configuration access across Core, Loader, Include and HMR**: rc.11 Core owns raw `Fiber.config`, `internal/config(fiber, next)`, `internal/commit` and awaited `internal/update(config, next)`. Root-fiber candidate resolution remains available without a plugin schema. Local `rawConfig`, `resolveConfig(candidate)` and `effectiveConfig` accessors retain the DSH consumer API. Fiber caches the object passed to activation or a successful update that keeps the instance; candidate resolution is pure, failed or superseded updates cannot replace the cache, and volatile updates retain references. Loader resolves only entry roots and excludes Group/Include tree carriers, so nested `!!js` expressions wait for their own injections. Include retains its tree-carrier marker, writer and patches, and HMR transfers raw config through the accessors. Covered by `scripts/cordis-config-access.spec.ts`, `scripts/cordis-core-lifecycle.spec.ts` and the boot/HMR suites.
- **V16 · `cordis/package.json` publishes `src`**: added `src` to the `files` list, joining the other eight vendored packages. Cordis declares `"./src/*": "./src/*"` in its exports, so a tarball without `src` publishes an export map pointing at absent files; the release change judgement also reads `files` to decide whether a diff reaches the payload, and a package whose only published paths are build output has no tracked path to match.
- **V17 · `@deepseek-ai` rescope**: every vendored manifest `name`, every internal dependency entry among the vendored set, and every module specifier that reaches them use the scoped names in the manifest table's `npm name` column. Directory names, version numbers, and dependency ranges are unchanged, and no upstream runtime identifier is renamed — `Symbol.for('schemastery')` and Schemastery's `vendor:` metadata field keep their upstream values. Re-apply with `pnpm run rescope-vendor --apply` after a sync; the table's two name columns are the mapping, restated for consumers in [docs/rescope.md](../docs/rescope.md).
- **V18 · Entry `disabled` interpolation in `loader/src/config/entry.ts`**: a `disabled: !!js` expression evaluates against the loader context at every mount decision; the raw node stays in the options, so write-back keeps the `!!js` form. `disabled` is the only interpolated metadata field. Covered by `packages/boot/app-boot/tests/user-patches.spec.ts` and `apps/cli/tests/windows-shell.spec.ts`.
- **V22 · Volatile config across `cosmokit`, `schemastery`, `cordis`, and `loader`**: Cosmokit supplies immutable references and framework-owned commits; `deepEqual` treats two references as equal, propagates strict comparison into arrays, compares every array slot with holes treated as undefined, handles cycles conservatively, compares URLs by normalized href, and compares other opaque objects by identity in strict mode. Schemastery adds `.volatile()`, optional/default inference, placement validation without eager lazy-schema expansion (a lazy inner is validated once when built), metadata-free serialized node compatibility, serialized metadata, reference-aware simplification, unsupported volatile values reported as `ValidationError` with their path, and `.default()` accepting the raw input type `Partial<S>` because a volatile field makes the output type carry references. Loader's save path calls `simplify` with its schema receiver (`unparse.call`), an independent fix for the unbound-`this` call. Cordis exports consumer types without changing Fiber lifecycle. Loader compares raw options strictly in `Entry.update`; for a config-only change on an active fiber it calls the pure `equalExceptVolatile` function in `config/diff.ts`, which narrows the Standard Schema to Schemastery's `Schema` type (a new type-only `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` dependency of `loader`) and recursively skips fixed volatile paths using schema metadata without executing config hooks or validation. Missing or null object nodes compare using their declared defaults, including nodes without volatile descendants; schema backedges retain raw comparison. Entry passes its actual schema and preserves ordinary context and custom-update lifecycles. For a volatile-only change, `Entry._commitVolatile` takes the canonical fiber `entry.fiber.ctx.fiber` (`Entry.fiber` holds the registry wrapper), re-parses the raw config through `Fiber.resolveConfig()`, compares ordinary effective values, commits references and emits the instance-local `loader/volatile-update` declared in `loader/src/index.ts`; a changed ordinary effective value falls back to the ordinary remount, and an invalid candidate is logged while the raw config stays retained for the next activation. Cosmokit provides reference enumeration and commits, and `simplify` is called with its schema receiver. The package READMEs document these additions; schema tests live in `scripts/volatile-config.spec.ts`, Loader runtime and real-file tests in `scripts/loader-volatile-update.spec.ts`, and code replacement tests in the HMR module suite.
- **V23 · `loader/src/config/entry.ts` module identity**: retains each entry's raw import result as `moduleNamespace`, before plugin export normalization. HMR matches that object to Node's cached module namespace and updates it after a successful reload. `EntryTree.import()` keeps its existing arguments and return value; `loader/README.md` documents the additive field.
- **V24 · `timer/locale/{en,zh}.json` display metadata**: local English and Chinese titles and descriptions for the Settings plugin inventory. `timer/package.json` exports and publishes these locale resources.
- **V25 · Loader lifecycle slice from Cordis v4.0.0-rc.11**: entry updates await context patches, Fiber updates and disabled-entry disposal; isolation uses `Impl.ctx` and maintains `Impl.isolate` during transfers; the `Entry.init()` observer handles both activation outcomes. Group and Include return their child-update work. The existing writer receives `internal/commit` with schema-bound simplification. A local dependency refresh before a combined context/config update prevents activation against stale isolation bindings. Loader, Include and HMR keep their manifest baselines apart from the slices recorded in this log. Failed fibers require an explicit update after correcting their input or dependencies. Core retains the effect hardening in V6; rc.11 owns dependency teardown ordering and superseded-activation handling.
- **V26 · Satori PR #416 source subset**: adds `plugin-im-core`, `plugin-im-adapter-lark`, `satori-protocol`, and `satori-element` from the manifest pin, with independently pinned `element`, `http`, and `fetch-file` dependencies. Local source imports and type-only specifiers follow V4 and V17. The core ecosystem metadata uses `im` and `@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-im-*`; runtime service names, events, and `satori:` URLs retain their upstream names. README code examples use the scoped imports. Package READMEs are copied only where upstream supplies a package README; root Satori documentation is not duplicated into packages. Element comes from its independent repository: npm 0.3.0 metadata still points to an older WebUI commit with an incompatible export API.
- **V27 · IM package set in `vendor/`**: four packages come from the Satori pin recorded in the manifest — `satori-element/`, `plugin-im-core/`, `plugin-im-adapter-lark/` and `plugin-im-adapter-qq/` — with independently pinned `element`, `http` and `fetch-file` dependencies. Their upstream sources are replaced wholesale (V28–V31), so no upstream IM source is copied verbatim: the platform routes, wire envelopes, protobuf/JSON gateway formats and the token endpoints carry over, the rendering pipeline does not. Service names, events and `satori:` URLs keep their upstream names.
- **V28 · `satori-element/` is the element vocabulary**: upstream factories and aliases, the global `JSX` declaration and the blanket re-export of `cordis-element` are replaced by a typed `ElementMap` / `VariantMap` / `Element<K>` overlay over the unchanged runtime (`vocabulary.ts`), the block/inline category and tier table (`elements.ts`), the typed `h` factory with an automatic JSX runtime (`factory.ts`), `normalize()` (root `<message>`, flow-container wrapping, envelope and content-model validation; `normalize.ts`), `variantsOf()` / `variantKey()` (`variants.ts`), the plain projection `toText()` (`text.ts`) and `fromMarkdown()` (`markdown.ts`). `fromMarkdown()` is a real mdast + GFM converter (`mdast-util-from-markdown`, `micromark-extension-gfm`, `mdast-util-gfm`): headings, emphasis, deletion, inline code, fenced code, lists with `checked`, blockquote, thematic break, tables with alignment, links and images; HTML stays literal text, a soft line break becomes `<br>`, and a paragraph holding only an image yields a block `img`. Plain strings are literal text — markup is parsed only by the explicit `parse()`.
- **V29 · `plugin-im-core/` is the IM engine**: upstream `message.ts` (`MessageEncoder`), the `Methods`/`features`/`supports(name)` surface, the component service and the protocol dependency are gone. `protocol.ts` holds the public types (`Login`, `User`, `Status`, `Meta`, `WebSocket`, `ChatRef`, `Target`, `UserRef`, `MessageRef`, `InboundMessage`, the `ButtonEvent` augmentation). A mode renders what its registry registers — the tag plus the variants its handler declares — and adapters say nothing about a chat. `mode.ts` holds `defineMode` and the `LimitKey` table, `registry.ts`, `fallback.ts` and `transform.ts` the transform engine and the core fallback table, `degradation.ts` the priced mode score, `directives.ts` the `prefer-streamable-mode` / `prefer-expressive-mode` content directives, `resource.ts` the `ResourceRef` walk and the LRU resource cache (bounded concurrency, single upload per cache key), `stream.ts` the stream scheduler with its `patch` / `edit` / `append` drivers, `errors.ts` the platform taxonomy (`PlatformError` kinds, retry hints, `published`) and `testing.ts` with `testing/` the offline testkit (`FakeAdapter`, the shared corpus, conformance, goldens). `bot.ts` splits the public `Bot` from the implementer `Adapter`: one pipeline (`normalize` → `transform` → `prepare` → `serialize` → `sendPayload`) for every adapter, mode resolution per publication, retries, `PartialSendError`, `edit`/`delete`/`stream` over the same handle, and the awaited `satori/receive` intake gate. `session.ts` keeps the slim `Session` envelope with its `onClick` callback registry, and `internal.ts` serves the `satori:` routes plus the `/_api/:name` and `/_tmp/:id` passthroughs.
- **V30 · `plugin-im-adapter-lark/` is rewritten for the protocols above**: `config.ts` is the Schemastery schema (`platform` selects the OpenAPI host and the reported platform; `cardStreaming`, `callbacks`, `allowAtAll` and the long-connection limits), `api/client.ts` the typed REST client (message create/reply/update/patch/delete/get/list, chat get, image and file upload, resource download, reactions) over an injected transport, `api/token.ts` the tenant token with a 30-minute refresh window and a single-flight refresh, `api/cardkit.ts` the CardKit entity routes, `api/events.ts` the schema-2.0 event envelopes and the `LarkReferrer` contract. `errors.ts` maps the platform code table onto `PlatformError` with the `published` verdict, and `230075` stays a `limit` so the stream scheduler resolves a refused edit by recall-and-resend. `ws.ts` is the protobuf long connection (gateway handshake, fragment reassembly, heartbeats, ACK only after intake, immediate answer for `card.action.trigger`), `bot.ts` the adapter shell, `modes/post.ts` and `modes/card.ts` the two modes with their escapers, `prepare.ts` the upload stage, `send.ts` the create/reply/edit/recall routes, `stream.ts` the CardKit `patch` driver, and `decode.ts` the inbound decoder and the chat-kind mapping.
- **V31 · `plugin-im-adapter-qq/` is ported for the protocols above**: `config.ts` is the Schemastery schema with two explicit decisions — `transport: 'ws' | 'none'` (a REST-only client never opens a gateway session) and `passive.seqBase` starting at 2, because `msg_seq` is deduplicated per `(msg_id, msg_seq)` and koishi's adapter starts at 1 — plus configurable `baseUrl` and `tokenUrl`. `token.ts` caches the app access token, refreshes at `expires_in − 60 s`, refreshes single-flight and keeps serving a still-valid token when a refresh fails. `api.ts` is the typed v2 REST client (gateway, group/C2C messages, files, recall, interaction acknowledgement, C2C `stream_messages`) with self-describing `group:<openid>` / `user:<openid>` addressing. `errors.ts` maps the platform code table, the `304…` quota family and the HTTP-status fallbacks onto `PlatformError`. `passive.ts` owns the passive-reply windows and the per-event `msg_seq` budget, and reports the replies a stream may still spend. `modes/text.ts`, `modes/markdown.ts` and `keyboard.ts` render the two `msg_type` bodies and the custom keyboard, `prepare.ts` uploads media, `send.ts` publishes with the passive bookkeeping and the dedupe retry, `stream.ts` the C2C `append` driver, `ws.ts` the JSON gateway state machine and `decode.ts` the inbound decoder plus the chat-lifecycle events.
- **V32 · Generated Feishu API subset**: `plugin-im-adapter-lark/src/types/` is generated and ignored by Git. `scripts/gen-vendor-im-types.ts` fetches the upstream files fixed by `scripts/vendor-im/upstream.json`, verifies SHA-256, and applies the import and type-closure transformations. The root `postinstall` runs it before all local and CI source checks; `pnpm run gen:vendor-im` regenerates explicitly and `--check` detects drift. Verified inputs are cached under `.cache/vendor-im/`; a changed digest or a failed download stops installation instead of accepting a moving platform definition. Package `src` publication includes the generated files, and tarball checks run after generation.
- **V33 · IM dependencies and build integration**: HTTP uses the repository's `undici@8.11.2`; `fetch-file` uses `mime-types@^3.0.2` / `@types/mime-types@^3.0.1` and keeps separate node/browser runtime builds; `satori-element` declares the markdown parser closure. The vendored manifests reference each other with `workspace:~`, and every vendored tsconfig extends the repo-root `tsconfig.base.json` and compiles under its strict settings — the upstream nullability, catch and function-variance relaxations are not carried over. HTTP serializes WebSocket headers as an entry object, and adapters send multipart bodies through the `undici` `FormData` class (V38).
- **V34 · Awaited intake in `plugin-im-core/src/{index,bot}.ts`**: the awaited `satori/receive` event and `Bot.receive()`. `dispatch()` stays synchronous; the Feishu WebSocket receiver awaits intake consumers before sending a success ACK, then publishes ordinary observer events. An intake rejection withholds the ACK without discarding the caller's durable state.
- **V35 · Connection ownership in `plugin-im-core` and the adapters**: each run owns its cancellation, retry timers, sockets, initialization, heartbeat, token refresh and event-processing promises. Stop aborts setup and connections, cancels timers, closes late sockets, clears fragments and awaits tracked work; concurrent starts retain only the latest controller. Initial retry exhaustion marks the bot offline, an established connection keeps supervised reconnects, and an initialization failure can never mark the bot online. Token refresh logs no credentials and closes the connection on failure so supervision can reauthenticate.
- **V36 · Platform wire validation and limits**: the Lark long connection validates the selected envelope and application identity, ignores unselected event families, and bounds frame bytes, fragment counts, partial messages and outstanding intake operations through configuration; fragments expire, identical duplicate segments do not advance completion, and conflicting segments are rejected. The QQ gateway validates every frame, serializes dispatches in arrival order while heartbeats stay independent, and treats a missing `HEARTBEAT_ACK` as a half-open socket. Both clients answer a platform-declared failure with a typed error carrying the platform code.
- **V37 · Lark card entities, media and reactions**: `api/cardkit.ts` covers what the generated subset does not — entity creation from complete card JSON 2.0, sending that entity once as an `interactive` message or reply, replacing the whole card, per-element content/patch/insert/delete and the settings route — with the caller owning each entity's strictly increasing `sequence`. Uploads go through the image and file routes and require a platform key; a media message is sent once with a caller-owned `uuid` and an authorized reply target. `createReaction()` adds one catalogue emoji (a repeated create is harmless) and `deleteReaction()` reads the message's reactions first and deletes only the one this application owns, because the platform deletes by reaction identity rather than by emoji.
- **V38 · Multipart bodies in `http/src/index.ts`**: a `FormData` built by Node's global class is rebuilt in the `undici` package's own class before dispatch, and `encodeRequest` recognizes either class. `undici@8.11.2` is a different implementation from the fetch built into Node, so its `fetch` coerced a foreign `FormData` to a string: every multipart request went out as `[object FormData]` with `content-type: text/plain`, and Feishu answered `234001 Invalid request param` for each image or file upload. Covered by `scripts/vendor-http.spec.ts`, which drives one multipart request against a loopback server.
- **V39 · Mode selection, content directives and the mode score in `plugin-im-core`**: no configuration knob and no caller picks a mode; an adapter declares its modes and their order (`Adapter.modeOrder`) and `Bot.send`/`Bot.render` resolve one per publication — every candidate mode is transformed once and the one losing the least wins, the declared order breaking a tie. Two content directives narrow the candidates: a root-level `<meta name="prefer-streamable-mode" value="true" />` keeps only modes with a stream driver (implied by `Bot.stream`, which also keeps the mode fixed for the whole stream), and `prefer-expressive-mode` keeps the broadest mode by counting the `element.*` keys it renders natively. Losing content is priced rather than counted (media, mentions and mid-message structure cost more than inline formatting, a dropped element always costs most, a folded panel costs nothing), so losing bold never weighs as much as losing a picture, and a mode can override one price or forbid a loss. `RenderResult` reports the resolved mode.
- **V40 · `<fallback>` replaced the capability layer as the way content adapts to a platform**: `@deepseek-ai/satori-element` gained the `fallback` element (each direct child is one ranked candidate, a JSX fragment counting as one) and its internal `case` node, `normalize` turns candidates into `case` children normalized as content of the element the `<fallback>` stands in, and renderers now write alternatives instead of asking what a platform supports. `RenderEngine.render` picks the first candidate whose whole subtree is native, else the last candidate with the usual lowering, records the choice in `RenderReport.fallbacks` (and charges a later candidate in `degradationScore`), so `<fallback><title>…</title><h3>…</h3></fallback>` names both the expressive and the plain spelling of one message. Nothing in the engine consults per-chat state: a mode renders what its registry registers, a declared variant included.
- **V41 · The IM capability layer is gone, not deprecated**: `plugin-im-core/src/capabilities.ts` (`ChatFacts`, `FactCache`, `LearnedFact`, `Support`, `Level`, `Capabilities`, the `element.*`/`message.*`/`limit.*` key vocabulary, `evaluateCapabilities`, `mergeCapabilities`), `Bot.supports`/`support`/`capabilities`, `Adapter.facts`, `Mode.operations`, `HandlerOptions.available`, `PlatformError.facts` and `RenderContext.caps`/`supports` were removed together with the Lark chat probe (`facts.ts`) and the QQ passive-window facts. What a platform allows is now the platform's answer at the moment of the call: a refusal rejects with the classified `PlatformError`, and content that must degrade says so with `<fallback>`. `LimitKey` moved to `mode.ts`, a mode owns its element budget in `assemble`/`check`, and `MessageStream.abort()` reports whether a recall removed the published message. The IM consumers (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-im` and its plugins) stopped querying capabilities: a renderer reads the stream strategy it was handed and writes alternatives.
- **V42 · `button[type=input]` and the Lark card mode**: the "a click sends this text as the user" button variant is `input` throughout the vocabulary (`ElementMap.button`, `VariantMap`, the core fallback, the QQ keyboard's `action.type 2` encoding). The Lark card mode does not render it: a card button can only answer with a callback, so the variant stays undeclared and the core fallback renders the label plus the text.
- **V43 · Stream diagnostics in `plugin-im-core/src/stream.ts`**: an intermediate state that cannot be rendered, a refused open and a refused tick are dropped as before — close renders again and reports — but each now logs once through the host logger inside its own `try`/`catch`, so a turn that publishes nothing says why instead of looking like a stream with nothing to say, and diagnostics never break a stream. The card mode declares the `action` variant of `<button>` under the same `callbacks` switch, which is what keeps a summary turn's stop button live.
- **V44 · `plugin-im-core/src/bot.ts` status setter reads the `bots` registry without an inject**: `set status` announced `login-updated` through `this.ctx.bots`, but `bots` is a mixin of the `satori` service, so a fiber that no longer injects that service — the teardown of a failed boot — threw `cannot get property "bots" without inject` from `Bot.offline()` and buried the real startup error. It now reads `this.ctx.get('satori')?.bots`, which answers `undefined` without the inject.
- **V45 · `plugin-im-adapter-qq/src/bot.ts` gateway host rewrite**: `gatewayUrl()` replaced the `api.sgroup.qq.com` substring of the `GET /gateway` answer with the configured REST host. In sandbox that answer is already `wss://sandbox.api.sgroup.qq.com/websocket`, and the substring occurs inside `sandbox.api.…`, so the result was `wss://sandbox.sandbox.api.sgroup.qq.com/websocket` — no DNS name answers it and every socket closed with 1006, leaving `sandbox: true` unusable. The rewrite now parses both URLs and assigns `host` only when it differs, so a host the endpoint chose for itself stays as served. Covered by `tests/bot.spec.ts`.
- **V46 · `plugin-im-adapter-qq` full-mode group messages**: a bot with 接收所有消息 switched on receives every group message as `GROUP_MESSAGE_CREATE` instead of `GROUP_AT_MESSAGE_CREATE`, so `decodeDispatch` published nothing for `@`-mentions in that group. The event now decodes through the same path, with two differences the platform dictates: the body keeps the `<@…>` mention in place, and `mentions` never carries the bot itself, so the bot's own `union_openid` — which `READY` does not report — is read once from `GET /users/@me` (`QQBot.ensureIdentity`, `QqApi.getSelf`). Only a body that mentions the bot is `mentions.self`, so background chatter stays unaddressed; a failed identity read is reported and leaves the message unaddressed rather than guessing. Covered by `tests/decode.spec.ts`.
- **V47 · `plugin-im-adapter-qq` renders code as code**: the markdown mode registered neither `code` nor `pre`, so an inline span lost its backticks and a code block arrived as an escaped paragraph — indentation and blank lines collapsed, and every `#`, `*` and `|` carried a backslash. Both tags are native now: `code` becomes a backtick span and `pre` a fenced block whose body is a new `QqNode` kind, `verbatim`, which `assemble` copies into the content without escaping, collapsing or the `\u200B` padding that keeps blank lines alive. A table the core fallback can lay out as a monospace grid follows the same path, so a narrow table reaches the chat as an aligned fenced grid — QQ markdown renders no tables of its own. Covered by `tests/markdown.spec.ts` and the mode goldens.
- **V48 · `plugin-im-adapter-qq` streaming chunk body, mode and stream identity**: `stream_messages` names a chunk's text `content_raw`, not the `content` of an ordinary send; it takes the whole state with `input_mode: 'replace'`, as its own examples do; and its first answer returns the streamed message's identity in `id` — there is no `stream_msg_id` field. The adapter sent `content`, a hand-computed suffix with `input_mode: 'append'`, and read `answer.stream_msg_id`, and none of the three mistakes shows in the status: a chunk with no text is still accepted, and a live 单聊 stream answered `remain_msg_len: 0` for a message that had just taken five characters, which turned every later append into a `shape` violation. `sendChunk` now sends the full state with `replace` and takes the stream id from the first answer's `id`, and `assertRoom` reads a zero `remain_msg_len` as "not measured" rather than as "no room", so the platform's own refusal decides. Verified against the live 单聊 stream that previously broke. Covered by `tests/stream.spec.ts`.
- **V49 · `plugin-im-core` opens a stream in the broadest streamable mode**: `Bot.stream()` resolved its mode with `preferredModeId()` — the *first* declared mode that has a driver. An adapter whose cheapest mode also streams therefore spent the whole turn in it (`text` before `markdown` on QQ), and because a streamed message fixes its `content_type` at the first chunk and can never switch, a streamed answer lost every emphasis, code block and link while the same answer sent once kept them. `streamMode()` resolves the same question the content directives ask — `prefer-streamable-mode` narrows the pool to the modes with a driver, `prefer-expressive-mode` takes the broadest of those — which needs no content, because breadth is a property of the mode registry. `preferredModeId()` remains only as the stand-in mode for a `MessageRef` this bot did not send. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-core/tests/bot.spec.ts`.
- **V50 · `plugin-im-adapter-qq` markdown mode composes a fence inside a list item or a quote**: `mapRuns` keeps a verbatim node out of the text run so nothing collapses the blank lines of a code block, which also kept it out of the prefix a list item or a block quote puts on every line it owns. A `<pre>` inside either was emitted mid-line (`- 第二项```), so the fence never opened, and the container's own marker ended up glued to the closing fence (` ```>`), swallowing every following block into that code block. `flattenRuns` flattens rendered children into lines first — text runs formatted, code lines untouched — and the two handlers prefix every line; `mapRuns` keeps its other callers. Covered by `tests/markdown.spec.ts`.
- **V51 · `plugin-im-adapter-lark` keeps code spans verbatim and leaves `= …` text alone**: card markdown escaped every `<` of user text as `&#60;`, inline code spans included, and neutralised any line that started with `=`. The platform decodes no entity inside code — a card showed `Result&#60;DsResponse, DsResponse>` — and does not consume a backslash before `=` — `= 104 B, align 8` arrived as `\= 104 B, align 8`. `cardCodeSpan` now leaves its body verbatim like `cardFence` (a span cannot open a tag, and the entity would only reach the reader), and `escapeCardBlockStart` neutralises `=` only on a line that is nothing but `=` (a setext underline), so ordinary text keeps both characters. Covered by `tests/card.spec.ts`.
- **V52 · `plugin-im-adapter-qq` markdown escaper defuses block markers instead of escaping them**: the escaper wrote `\#`, `\-` and `1\.` ahead of a line-start marker, which only works if the platform honours CommonMark backslash escapes. QQ does for `\*` but not for these: a stress answer reached the chat with `1\.` and `\#general` showing the backslash, every numbered heading of it included. Inline metacharacters keep their backslash (`* _ ~`, backtick, brackets, angle brackets); a block marker (a list item, a heading, a quote, a rule) now takes a leading U+200B instead, which is invisible and keeps the marker from being read at line start at all. Covered by `tests/markdown.spec.ts` and the refreshed corpus goldens.
- **V53 · `plugin-im-adapter-lark` names the failures behind a rejected intake frame**: the long connection logs one line per frame it could not acknowledge, and the rejection it catches is an `AggregateError` over that frame's listeners whose own message is empty — every line therefore read `… retry: AggregateError` and named no listener, leaving one intake failure indistinguishable from the next. `describeIntakeFailure` unwraps it: each aggregated failure arrives with its `name` and its `code` (`ImError` carries `persistence`, `access`, `capacity`, …), which is what says whether admission failed in intake, in a session flush or in a renderer. The ACK behaviour is unchanged and stays covered by `tests/ws.spec.ts`.
- **V54 · `plugin-im-core` settles a stream it cannot recall instead of failing the turn**: `Scheduler.resend` recalled the streamed message and, when the platform refused the delete, threw `StreamLimitError` — so the last chunk was never sent with `input_state: 10` and the chat showed that message as generating forever. QQ refuses every `DELETE` of a streamed message (`40061001`), which made this the normal outcome as soon as an answer re-parsed mid-stream: a `**bold**` that completes changes the escaped prefix of a state, so the next state cannot be appended. A stream that cannot be recalled is now closed on the state it already shows, and the final state follows as a fresh message; `limitFail` settles the same way before it throws. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-core/tests/stream.spec.ts` and the QQ adapter's `tests/stream.spec.ts`.
- **V55 · `plugin-im-core` prices a moved element**: `degradationScore` charged `degraded`, `fallbacks` and `dropped`, but an element a mode lifted out of the message body (`RenderReport.moved`) was free. A platform whose plain-text body has no image syntax therefore tied with the mode that keeps the picture inline, and the declared order decided it — so every answer mixing text with a picture was split into text, picture, text. A moved element now costs `COST_PLAIN` each, which resolves such content to the mode that can keep it: content that interleaves nothing (a picture on its own, or text alone) still ties and keeps the cheaper declared order.
- **V56 · `plugin-im-adapter-qq` embeds a picture in the markdown body**: the `img` handler published every picture as its own `msg_type: 7` message, so a mixed answer reached the chat as three messages and spent three passive replies. QQ's markdown renders `![alt #Wpx #Hpx](…)` inline — both pixel dimensions are required, `0px` meaning the source size — and fetches the source itself, so the markdown mode now keeps the picture in its own body: `assemble` leaves a placeholder and `serialize` fills it with the uploaded `qqbot-media://` reference (`prepare` uploads it for the chat, so a public URL and a local file take one path). The text mode keeps the media message, and the picture stays inside its sentence rather than taking a paragraph of its own. Covered by `tests/markdown.spec.ts` and the refreshed markdown goldens.

- **V57 · `plugin-im-adapter-lark` hands a card's pictures back as images**: a card shows its pictures by `image_key`, and the decoder turned each one into the `[image]` text reference only, so a card's picture was never a media element — `im_read_image` on such a message answered "no media element" while the card text showed nothing but a placeholder. `walkCard` now collects the keys (with a picture's alternative text as its `alt`), `interactiveNodes` emits a real `img` whose `src` is `satori:<platform>/<selfId>/images/<image_key>`, and `LarkBot` serves that route through the new `LarkApi.getImage` (`GET /im/v1/images/{image_key}`). The platform hands such a key only to the application that sent the picture: another application's card answers `234008 The app is not the resource sender`, so the card's text stays the part every reader gets. Covered by `tests/card.spec.ts`.

### Resolver adaptations

Relative to the resolver source in Cordis `v4.0.0-rc.11`:

- **Web build imports:** `loader/src/resolve.ts` uses default imports for Node builtin modules to support the Web shell's browser externalization. The shell supplies its own module loader.
- **Package-scope cache keys:** `loader/src/resolve.ts` normalizes directory paths with `path.resolve()` before finding the package scope. A root config and a nested config in the same package therefore share the same cached resolver promise and helper-file write. Covered by `scripts/cordis-loader-resolve.spec.ts`.

## IM baseline

The IM packages are transport libraries: they render, publish and decode, and they carry no harness session dependency. The Cordis fork they run on is the one vendored here, with its own lifecycle and Loader patches.

The [IM decision](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-10-12-im-automation-sessions.md) owns the automation design. The Lark resource route (`/messages/:messageId/resources/:fileKey`) is bot-scoped and therefore cannot shadow the shared `/_api/` route; retained native operations reach the platform through `bot.internal` (the generated route tree) or the typed client in `src/api/`. Offline tests do not establish real Feishu authentication, required permissions, ACK deadlines, redelivery, thread containers, reply placement, or UUID deduplication behavior.

## Sync procedure

To update a vendored package from upstream:

1. In the upstream workspace, note `git rev-parse HEAD` of the relevant submodule.
2. Copy the package's `src/` (and `bin.js`, `README.md`, `LICENSE` if changed) over the vendored directory.
3. Re-apply the local modifications listed above (or drop them if upstream made them unnecessary — update the log either way).
4. Update the version and commit hash in the manifest table.
5. Run `pnpm install && pnpm run test && pnpm run build` at the repo root.
